summary: The Advanced Computing Facility is the University of Edinburgh's high-performance computing data centre south of Edinburgh, operated by EPCC. It hosts the UK national supercomputer ARCHER2 and other research systems, and its grid capacity was upgraded from 8 MW to 38 MW in 2023 to support future systems including the planned UK exascale supercomputer, to be housed in a new circa GBP31m wing.
maturity_explanation: Long-established operating university HPC facility; hosts ARCHER2 (in service since 2021) per EPCC and University of Edinburgh publications.

phases.phase_name: Existing ACF computer rooms (ARCHER2 and other systems)
Exascale wing (new build for UK exascale system)
phases.description: Circa GBP31m wing built under the Edinburgh and South East Scotland City Region Deal; exascale project cancelled by UK Government in 2024 then reinstated with ~GBP750m funding; first-phase installation reported due from 2025.

latest_development.headline: UK exascale supercomputer project reinstated for the ACF after 2024 funding U-turn; new wing to house the system.
